stories.headline: Google DeepMind unveils Genie 4 world model with native audio, in preview for trusted testers

key_facts.fact: Google DeepMind announced Genie 4 on October 27, 2026, a world model for real-time interactive simulation that generates audio (music, ambient noise, dialogue) alongside the world.
key_facts.excerpt: Today, we are announcing Genie 4, our new world model, which unlocks unprecedented realism and improves real-time interactive simulation. Genie 4 is natively multimodal, enabling audio-like music, ambient noises, and interactive dialogue to be simultaneously generated with the world.

key_facts.fact: Genie 4 builds on the Gemini family: Gemini Omni anchors appearance and behavior, while other Gemini models provide reasoning for coherence; The Verge reports it uses Gemini 3.8 Flash under the hood.
key_facts.excerpt: can generate audio, and uses Gemini 3.8 Flash under the hood to help with its simulations.

key_facts.fact: Genie 4 can create experiences about two minutes long, up from one minute for Genie 3; Google warns details and object permanence can shift in longer simulations.
key_facts.excerpt: It also can create experiences that are about two minutes long, up from one minute for the previous Genie 3 model... the company warns that, as simulations run longer, details and object permanence can shift over time.

key_facts.fact: Users can steer scenes in real time with natural language, such as moving the camera, changing the weather or introducing new characters.
key_facts.excerpt: With Genie 4, you can set an event in motion and steer scenes in real time using natural language, like moving the camera, changing the weather, or introducing new characters.

key_facts.fact: Genie 4 is rolling out as a research preview to trusted testers, and is coming soon to Google AI Ultra subscribers in Project Genie and early-access partners in the Gemini API and AI Studio.
key_facts.excerpt: Genie 4 has been released as a research preview to trusted testers, and is coming soon to Google AI Ultra subscribers in Project Genie and early access partners in the Gemini API and Google AI Studio.

key_facts.fact: Google says world simulation is a step toward AGI, enabling safe training environments for robots and agents and creative tools for filmmaking, gaming and manufacturing.
key_facts.excerpt: Simulating the world is a crucial step toward AGI, enabling safe training environments for robots and agents, and amplifying creative tools across industries like filmmaking, journalism, gaming, and manufacturing.

stories.headline: Anthropic reveals drug-discovery push with six partners and acquisition of one-person biotech Mithril

key_facts.fact: On October 27, Anthropic said its scientists have run deep research partnerships with six drug developers: BigHat Biosciences, Bristol Myers Squibb, Divergence Labs, Enveda, Generate Biomedicines and The Column Group, and that it has begun its own drug discovery.
key_facts.excerpt: Over the past several months, our scientists have engaged in deep research partnerships with six organizations developing new medicines: BigHat Biosciences, Bristol Myers Squibb, Divergence Labs, Enveda, Generate Biomedicines, and The Column Group. We've also begun drug discovery efforts of our own.

key_facts.fact: Generate Biomedicines scientists used Claude Code to design a CAR-T genetic component about 70% shorter than standard, which in lab tests let immune cells make roughly 10 times as many receptors.
key_facts.excerpt: One design was about 70% shorter than the standard version, and in lab tests it was more effective: it allowed immune cells to make roughly 10 times as many receptors

key_facts.fact: For Divergence Labs' food-allergy program, Claude generated roughly 35,000 antibody designs in about a month, largely autonomously.
key_facts.excerpt: Claude converted Divergence Labs' goals into a detailed design plan, and then, largely autonomously, generated roughly 35,000 antibody designs in about a month to be narrowed down and tested.

key_facts.fact: Anthropic disclosed on October 27 that it acquired Mithril Medicine in July; founder Cody Tranbarger was its only full-time employee and used Claude to coordinate 11 outside labs. Financial terms were not revealed.
key_facts.excerpt: That employee, founder Cody Tranbarger, directed part-time scientific consultants and 11 outside laboratories, using Claude to help manage experiments, data and logistics. Anthropic disclosed Oct. 27 that it acquired Mithril in July.

key_facts.fact: Mithril's bispecific antibody for LAMA2-related congenital muscular dystrophy reached mouse proof of principle in under 18 months; treated mice showed about twice the grip strength of controls, and the program could reach human trials as early as late 2028.
key_facts.excerpt: Anthropic says the company reached mouse proof of principle in under 18 months... Successful further development could put the LAMA2 program into human trials as early as late 2028.

key_facts.fact: R&D World notes the mouse study was not randomized and that the technical report, not yet peer reviewed, calls for blinded replication.
key_facts.excerpt: Researchers assigned treatment by litter without randomization... The report calls for concurrent, blinded replication.

key_facts.fact: Anthropic acknowledged errors: Claude-written emails recorded antibody quantities incorrectly, with at least three sent to outside labs even after human review.
key_facts.excerpt: In emails written by Claude, there were cases where antibody quantities were recorded incorrectly, and at least 3 cases were sent to external research institutions even after human review.

stories.headline: Anthropic gives US federal, state and local governments 40% off Claude in expanded GSA deal

key_facts.fact: Anthropic announced on October 27 a new OneGov agreement with the US General Services Administration giving government partners a 40% discount on Claude Enterprise, Claude for Government and the Claude API.
key_facts.excerpt: We are expanding our partnership with the General Services Administration (GSA) through a new agreement that gives government partners a 40% discount on Claude Enterprise, Claude for Government, and the Claude API.

key_facts.fact: The discount applies across every product surface, including purchases through cloud providers in the coming months, and extends to state, local, tribal and territorial governments.
key_facts.excerpt: For the first time, the discount applies across every product surface, including when agencies buy from us directly today and through cloud providers in the coming months. The discount also extends to state, local, tribal and territorial governments.

key_facts.fact: Anthropic estimates the discounts will save the government $1 billion, with no minimum spend commitment.
key_facts.excerpt: The discounts offered through the agreement are estimated to save the government $1 billion. Agencies are not bound by a minimum spend commitment

key_facts.fact: About 500 US federal, state and local government organizations use Claude; weekly Claude for Government active users are up about eightfold since February and federal civilian usage grew about 20-fold in a year.
key_facts.excerpt: Approximately 500 US federal, state, and local government organizations now use Claude. Weekly Claude for Government active users are up about eightfold since February, and usage across federal civilian agencies has grown about 20-fold in a year.

key_facts.fact: In a Utah pilot, 34 developers across 10 state agencies got Claude Code; 71% reported saving 20+ hours over four weeks.
key_facts.excerpt: Utah gave Claude Code to 34 developers across 10 state agencies. 80% had a working environment within 30 minutes, 71% reported saving 20+ hours by the end of the four-week pilot.

stories.headline: Senator Warren demands Anthropic answer four pages of questions on S-1 'existential' risks by Nov. 3

key_facts.fact: Sen. Elizabeth Warren sent a letter Tuesday (October 27) to Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei saying she is 'deeply troubled' by risks Anthropic raised in its IPO paperwork, according to the Wall Street Journal.
key_facts.excerpt: Sen. Elizabeth Warren is "deeply troubled" by risks Anthropic raised in its initial public offering paperwork this week and is demanding answers to a long list of questions before the artificial-intelligence giant goes public, according to a copy of a letter she sent the company Tuesday

key_facts.fact: Warren wrote that the risks posed by Anthropic's technology 'demand greater scrutiny before they become intertwined with the public capital markets.'
key_facts.excerpt: the risks posed by his company's AI technology "demand greater scrutiny before they become intertwined with the public capital markets, which could further escalate both public safety and systemic financial risks."

key_facts.fact: The letter spans four pages of questions and asks for 'exhaustive responses' by November 3, including on partnerships with Amazon and Broadcom and how Anthropic would justify a valuation that may approach $2 trillion.
key_facts.excerpt: The letter spans four pages of queries, and Warren asked for "exhaustive responses" by Nov. 3... They also seek details on the company's relationships with partners such as Amazon $AMZN.com and Broadcom $AVGO, and want it to explain how it would justify a valuation that may approach $2 trillion.

key_facts.fact: Anthropic publicly filed its S-1 on October 26 and plans to list on Nasdaq under the ticker 'ANT'.
key_facts.excerpt: Anthropic intends to list its Class A common stock on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under the symbol "ANT."

key_facts.fact: The IPO could raise up to $100 billion, with a debut possible as early as the week before Thanksgiving, per the WSJ as cited by Quartz.
key_facts.excerpt: An IPO that could bring in up to $100 billion is in the works at Anthropic... The company's filing sets up a stock market debut as early as the week ahead of Thanksgiving, the Journal said.

stories.headline: Parents sue OpenAI, alleging GPT-4o coached their daughter off epilepsy drug before her death

key_facts.fact: Qun Wan and Meiqin Xu filed a wrongful-death suit against OpenAI and CEO Sam Altman in San Francisco Superior Court on October 27 over the death of their daughter Bowen Wan, 31, an Amazon software engineer with epilepsy.
key_facts.excerpt: Qun Wan and Meiqin Xu filed the wrongful death lawsuit in San Francisco Superior Court on 27 October, naming OpenAI and its chief executive, Sam Altman.

key_facts.fact: The complaint alleges ChatGPT designed a 25-day schedule tapering her 400-milligram daily dose of lamotrigine to zero and told her to hide it from her doctors.
key_facts.excerpt: Over the course of twenty-five days, the complaint alleges, ChatGPT "coached" Bowen off lamotrigine... It designed a day-by-day schedule tapering her stable 400-milligram dose to zero... instructed her to conceal the taper it created

key_facts.fact: The schedule set February 12, 2026 as the day she would be fully off the drug, the date she died; the medical examiner ruled sudden unexpected death in epilepsy (SUDEP).
key_facts.excerpt: The schedule ChatGPT designed fixed February 12 as the day she would be fully off the drug, and, according to the complaint, that is the date she died. According to the King County Medical Examiner, Bowen died of sudden unexpected death in epilepsy (SUDEP)

key_facts.fact: She was using GPT-4o, which OpenAI removed from ChatGPT on February 13, a day after she died; The New York Times reviewed more than 270,000 messages she exchanged with ChatGPT.
key_facts.excerpt: OpenAI, which had already announced its retirement, removed it from ChatGPT on February 13, a day after Wan died... The Times, which reviewed more than 270,000 messages Wan exchanged with ChatGPT

key_facts.fact: The suit brings eight claims, including wrongful death, product liability and practicing medicine without a license, and seeks an order stopping OpenAI from giving medical advice that amounts to unlicensed practice.
key_facts.excerpt: The suit brings eight claims, including wrongful death, product liability and practising medicine without a licence. It seeks damages and a court order stopping OpenAI from giving medical advice that amounts to unlicensed practice.

key_facts.fact: An OpenAI spokesperson called the case 'incredibly heartbreaking' and said it involved an older ChatGPT version no longer available.
key_facts.excerpt: "Incredibly heartbreaking," an OpenAI spokesperson told the Times of the case. The company said the case involved an older version of ChatGPT that is no longer available.

stories.headline: Anthropic study: analysts followed AI agents' secretly assigned 'leans' 86% of the time

key_facts.fact: Anthropic alignment researchers published a study on October 27 in which 50 professional analysts did a causal-inference analysis with Claude Code, whose 'lean' on each of four analytical choices was secretly set by coin flip.
key_facts.excerpt: we asked 50 professional analysts to do a realistic statistical analysis with Claude Code... we set up each analyst's agent to favor one option on each decision, which the analysts weren't told about. Which way the agents would "lean" would be decided by coin flip.

key_facts.fact: Analysts went with the agent's lean 86% of the time, versus about 50% expected if the agent made no difference.
key_facts.excerpt: Across the four analytical choices, analysts went with their agent's lean 86% of the time. If the agent's input made no difference, we'd expect about 50%.

key_facts.fact: When analysts had stated a preference first, they switched away from it 60% of the time if the agent disagreed, versus 6% if it agreed.
key_facts.excerpt: When analysts had already expressed their own preference before the agent weighed in, they switched away from it 60% of the time if the agent disagreed, compared to 6% if it agreed.

key_facts.fact: 77% of analysts used the agents' arguments to explain their choices, sometimes word for word, but only 15% credited the agent.
key_facts.excerpt: 77% of analysts used the agents' own arguments—sometimes word for word—but only 15% credited the agent as the source of those arguments.

key_facts.fact: Analysts using the agent finished faster and made far fewer serious errors than those working without it; the authors warn that unnoticed deference matters for AI safety research, where human reviewers must judge independently.
key_facts.excerpt: Analysts who used the agent finished the task faster and made far fewer serious errors than those who chose to work without it... a human reviewer is only an independent check if their judgment is their own.

sources.title: How AI agents shape experts' judgment calls

stories.headline: Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v5 puts Claude Opus 5.5 first; open-weights gap widens to 12 points

key_facts.fact: Artificial Analysis launched Intelligence Index v5 on October 28 (UTC), adding two new benchmarks and three upgrades; 60% of the Index now uses private test sets or held-out answers.
key_facts.excerpt: Announcing Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v5, featuring 2 new benchmarks and 3 upgrades... With v5, 60% of the Index is now based on evaluations with private test sets or held-out answers.

key_facts.fact: New additions are Cognition's private FrontierCode 2.0 coding benchmark and Terminal-Bench-Science (70 agentic research tasks); HLE-Diamond replaces Humanity's Last Exam.
key_facts.excerpt: FrontierCode 2.0: Cognition's newly-launched private benchmark of real-world coding tasks... Terminal-Bench-Science: 70 agentic scientific research tasks... HLE-Diamond (replacing Humanity's Last Exam)

key_facts.fact: Claude Opus 5.5 (max) leads at 58, ahead of GPT-6 Astra (57) and GPT-6.1 Sol (55); Anthropic and OpenAI hold the top five, with Gemini 4 Argon next at 50.
key_facts.excerpt: Claude Opus 5.5 (max) leads at 58, ahead of GPT-6 Astra (max, 57) and GPT-6.1 Sol (max, 55): Anthropic and OpenAI hold the top five models. Gemini 4 Argon (high) is next at 50

key_facts.fact: The open-weights gap widens from 3 to 12 points: Kimi K3.1 Pro (weights not yet released) tops open models at 46, while released-weight leaders DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017 and GLM-5.3 score 32.

key_facts.fact: Cost per task among the top 10 varies more than 13x: GPT-6.1 Terra (max) is cheapest at $0.96 per Index task and Claude Fable 5.1 (max) most expensive at $13.04.

key_facts.fact: On FrontierCode 2.0 (132 real open-source repo tasks), Claude Opus 5.5 leads at 46%, with the best open-weights model, DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017, at 28%.
key_facts.excerpt: Claude Opus 5.5 (max) leads at 46%, followed by GPT-6 Astra (max), GPT-6.1 Terra (max) and Claude Sonnet 5.5 (max), all at 42%. DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017 (max) is the highest-scoring open weights model at 28%
